title: Fin-R1: A Large Language Model for Financial Reasoning through Reinforcement Learning

task.value: Building a compact 7B reasoning LLM for financial scenarios that addresses fragmented data, opaque reasoning, and weak transferability in financial tasks.
task.quote: In response, we introduce Fin-R1, a reasoning LLM designed for financial scenarios. With a compact size of 7 billion parameters, Fin-R1 reduces deployment costs while addressing the aforementioned challenges.

architecture.value: Two-stage pipeline: data distillation with DeepSeek-R1 and filtering with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as judge to build Fin-R1-Data; then SFT on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct followed by GRPO with format and accuracy rewards (Qwen2.5-Max as accuracy evaluator).
architecture.quote: The model is first trained via SFT on Fin-R1-Data and is then optimized through GRPO with two reward functions, a format reward and an accuracy reward.

data.value: Fin-R1-Data: 60,091 bilingual (Chinese/English) CoT entries in four categories, built from FinanceQT, Finance-500K, FinanceIQ, FinPEE, Ant-Finance, FinCorpus, FinQA, ConvFinQA, TFNS, FinCUGE. No market price data or frequency.
data.quote: Fin-R1-Data consists of 60,091 bilingual (Chinese and English) entries, organized into four categories, as shown in Figure 3.

window.value: No dated period; evaluation on random 1,000-question samples per dataset (all if fewer), and a stratified 10% test subset of Finance-Instruct-500k.
window.quote: For Finance-Instruct-500k, we evaluate the performance various models on a custom 10% test subset, extracted via stratified sampling from the full dataset. For all other datasets, we randomly sample 1,000 questions for testing

models.value: Base model Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; DeepSeek-R1-671B for distillation; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as data-filtering judge; Qwen2.5-Max as RL accuracy evaluator; GPT-4o compared as judge.
models.quote: We adopt Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as the base model.

baselines.value: Eight LLMs: DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B/14B/32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, Qwen-2.5-7B/14B/32B-Instruct; plus ablations Fin-R1-SFT and Fin-R1-Zero.
baselines.quote: We compare our Fin-R1 against eight state-of-the-art LLMs, including (i) DeepSeek-R1; (ii) DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B; (iii) DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B; (iv) DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B; (v) DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B; (vi) Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct; (vii) Qwen-2.5-14B-Instruct; and (viii) Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct.

headline_result.value: Average score 75.2 across five financial benchmarks, second to DeepSeek-R1 (78.2); best on FinQA (76.0) and ConvFinQA (85.0).
headline_result.quote: Specifically, it achieves an average score of 75.2, ranking the second overall, and outperforms all models of similar size, with only a 3-point gap from the best-performing DeepSeek-R1 (78.2).

uncertainty.value: Only for judge-model selection: five repeated experiments per prompt strategy on 100 FinQA samples. No repeated runs or intervals reported for main benchmark results.
uncertainty.quote: We randomly select 100 sample instances from the FinQA dataset and conduct five repeated experiments for each prompt strategy to assess result stability.

limitations.value: Authors note GRPO alone produces incoherent outputs and SFT can only imitate demonstrations; future work to support multimodal financial data.
limitations.quote: A closer look at the model output (see Figure 9(a)) reveals that using GRPO alone for RL training often produces incoherent outputs.

release.quote: Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/SUFE-AIFLM-Lab/Fin-R1, and has already attracted over 700 stars.
